Definition: Magor-mis-Sabib, a symbolic name of Pashur
BiblicalUsage: Magor-missabib means terror on every side, and it is the new name Jeremiah gives Pashur in Jeremiah 20:3, after Pashur smote the prophet and put him in the stocks: the LORD hath not called thy name Pashur, but Magor-missabib. Pashur is told his name is changed, and the terror he made for others becomes his own.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a name like this one is a sentence: Pashur made himself a terror to the prophet, and God made him a terror to himself.
